findings.title: Two separate, non-shared finance-user managers ('bursar' and 'finance-users') in the same sidebar
findings.evidence: The 'bursar' nav page (SABursar -> SAStaffManager kind='bursar') reads/writes /api/bursars/ backed by the CoreBursar table (superadminDataController.getSuperBursars line 3697 CoreBursar.findAndCountAll; createSuperBursar line 3748 CoreBursar.create). The 'finance-users' nav page reads/writes /api/school/finance-users/ backed by the SchoolAdmin table (financeController.getFinanceUsers line 671 SchoolAdmin.findAll; createFinanceUser line 717 SchoolAdmin.create). Both create a User with role_id=bursar. The two lists never reflect each other.
findings.userImpact: A bursar created under 'Finance Users' does not appear under 'Bursars' and vice versa, even though both pages claim to manage bursars/finance staff and both can log a person in. An admin can create the same person twice, or block them in one screen while they stay active in the other, with no indication the two screens are different systems.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate to a single source of truth for finance staff (pick CoreBursar or SchoolAdmin), and back both nav pages with it, or clearly differentiate their purpose (e.g. 'Bursar HR record' vs 'finance login/access') and link them. At minimum, surface a warning when a person exists in the other store.
findings.backendTrace: /api/bursars/* (superadmin.js:309-314) -> CoreBursar; /api/school/finance-users/* (school.js:338-340) -> SchoolAdmin. Distinct tables, both gated to school_admin+superadmin, both tenant-scoped, but no cross-reference.

findings.title: System Integrity panel hardcodes SHA-256 / audit-trail / immutable-records trust claims
findings.evidence: IntegrityPanel renders a fixed 'System Integrity ACTIVE' shield with copy 'All transactions are securely logged and audited' and badges 'SHA-256 Hashed', 'Audit Trail Enabled', 'Immutable Records' (IntegrityPanel.jsx:23-37, FU_INTEGRITY_BADGES in finance.constants.js:83-87). None of these are driven by any backend signal; the only dynamic text is `${summary.txToday} transactions hashed today` which is always 0 (see fu-fabricated-finance-dashboards).
findings.userImpact: The admin is shown a security-assurance panel asserting transactions are SHA-256 hashed and tamper-evident with an immutable audit trail. There is no evidence in the codebase that finance transactions are hashed or stored immutably, so this is an unverifiable trust claim presented as fact.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the panel or replace the hardcoded badges with claims you can actually back (e.g. real audit-log row counts), and drop the always-zero 'transactions hashed today' line.
findings.backendTrace: N/A — static frontend content; no backend basis for the hashing/immutability claims.

summary: The classes-subjects slice (SAClasses.js, SASubjects.js, rendered for activePage 'classes'->SAClasses and 'subjects'->SASubjects) is largely solid and functional end-to-end for school_admin. All list/CRUD/toggle/delete operations and every assignment modal (students, subjects, teachers to classes; classes and teacher to subjects) call real backend endpoints under the superadmin router mounted at /api. Those routes use the shared gate sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])] (routes/superadmin.js:227-260), and every handler in superadminDataController.js enforces tenant isolation via scopedSchoolId(req) on create/list and denyCrossTenant(req,res,row.school_id,...) on every id-addressed read/update/delete/assign (verified lines 2359-2862). A school_admin cannot reach another school's class/subject by id (403), and create is force-pinned to the JWT school_id, ignoring any client school_id. Tenant isolation for this slice is correct. The one real defect: ClassForm fetches GET /api/class-subtypes/ (SAClasses.js:220) but that route is registered ONLY on the superadmin-gated sa sub-router (superadmin.js:196), so a school_admin gets 403, the .catch(()=>{}) swallows it, and the Class Subtype dropdown is permanently empty for school admins. Secondary UX issues: AssignSubjectTeacherModal always shows a success toast even when the subject has no class links (the update is a silent no-op), and the Class form exposes raw developer-ish numeric fields (Form Number, Academic Year ID) and many unlabeled-purpose fields.
workingWell: Classes list + Subjects list load real, tenant-scoped data: GET /api/classes/ and /api/subjects/ -> getSuperClasses/getSuperSubjects force where.school_id = scopedSchoolId(req) for non-superadmin (superadminDataController.js:2362-2364, 2470-2472), so a school_admin only ever sees its own rows.

Create/Update/Delete/Toggle for both classes and subjects are real and tenant-guarded: create pins school_id from token (createSuperClass:2413-2416, createSuperSubject:2492-2495) and ignores client-supplied school_id on edit; update/delete/toggle all call denyCrossTenant against the row's school_id before mutating (2437/2451/2460 and 2507/2521/2530).

All three class assignment modals are wired end-to-end and tenant-safe: assign-students (capacity-checked, scoped to cls.school_id at 2666-2674), assign-subjects (2707-2719), assign-multiple-teachers (max_teachers checked, 2735-2756); each loads current+available lists from real endpoints that filter members by the class's own school_id.

Both subject assignment modals work end-to-end: assign-classes (assignSubjectClasses:2777-2790) and assign-teacher (assignSubjectTeacher:2792-2805), with available-classes/teachers scoped to sub.school_id (2829, 2841).

Search is genuinely server-side (q param -> Op.like across name/code/form/category for classes, name/code/description for subjects, 2366-2369 / 2474-2477) with debounce (250ms) and pagination wired to the returned total; empty, loading, and error states all render (loadError branch and the 'No ... yet' / 'No ... match your search' empty rows).

Academic Year dropdown in ClassForm resolves correctly for school_admin: GET /api/school/academic-years/ exists on the school router (routes/school.js:199) and the form upgrades the raw academic_year_id number input to a real <select> when years load (SAClasses.js:282-290).
Response shape matches: successResponse spreads payload at top level (superadminDataController.js:42), so the frontend's r.classes / r.subjects / r.total reads are correct.
Tables are wrapped in .sa-table-wrap with overflow-x:auto (SA.css:929-934) and the shell ships @media(max-width:600px) blocks, so the grid scrolls rather than overflowing on mobile.

findings.title: Class Subtype dropdown is permanently empty for school_admin (endpoint is superadmin-only, 403 silently swallowed)
findings.evidence: SAClasses.js:220 ClassForm fetches req('GET','/api/class-subtypes/').then(...).catch(()=>{}). That route is registered ONLY on the superadmin-gated sub-router: routes/superadmin.js:196 `sa.get('/class-subtypes/', data.getClassSubtypes)` where sa.use(requireRole(['superadmin'])) (superadmin.js:112). Grep confirms no school-level class-subtypes route exists anywhere. For a school_admin the GET returns 403, the .catch swallows it, subtypes stays [], and the dropdown (SAClasses.js:269-272) shows only '— None —'.
findings.userImpact: A school admin opening Add/Edit Class can never pick a Class Subtype — the dropdown is always empty even when subtypes exist in the system. The field silently does nothing, with no error shown. The Subtype column in the table will therefore always read '—' for classes they create.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose a read-only class-subtypes list to school_admin: add `router.get('/class-subtypes/', sla, data.getClassSubtypes)` on the shared (sla) router in superadmin.js alongside the other school-level reads, OR point the ClassForm at an existing school-scoped reference endpoint. At minimum, surface the failure instead of swallowing it so the gap is visible.
findings.backendTrace: GET /api/class-subtypes/ -> routes/superadmin.js:196 (sa router, requireRole(['superadmin']) at line 112) -> getClassSubtypes (superadminDataController.js:~2319). Endpoint EXISTS but is role-gated to superadmin only; school_admin -> 403.

findings.title: Assigning a teacher to a subject with no class links is a silent no-op but reports success
findings.evidence: SASubjects.js:292-297 handleAssign POSTs /api/subjects/{id}/assign-teacher/ then unconditionally shows 'Teacher assigned to subject' on any 2xx. Backend assignSubjectTeacher (superadminDataController.js:2792-2805) does ClassSubject.update({teacher_id},{where:{subject_id}}) — it only touches existing class-subject links. If the subject is not yet assigned to any class, zero rows update and it returns success({}, 'Subject teacher updated').
findings.userImpact: A school admin picks a teacher for a subject that hasn't been attached to any class, sees a green success toast, but nothing was actually assigned. Reopening shows no teacher recorded. The modal label ('assigns to all classes linked to this subject') hints at this but the success message contradicts it, causing confusion.
findings.suggestedFix: Have the backend return the affected-row count and the frontend show 'No classes are linked to this subject yet — assign classes first' when zero rows were updated; or block/disable the Assign action until at least one class is linked.
findings.backendTrace: POST /api/subjects/:id/assign-teacher/ -> routes/superadmin.js:260 (sla gate) -> assignSubjectTeacher (superadminDataController.js:2792). Exists, tenant-guarded via denyCrossTenant(2797); behaves as a no-op when the subject has no ClassSubject rows.

findings.title: Class form exposes raw 'Academic Year ID' / 'Form Number' inputs and many ambiguous fields with no guidance
findings.evidence: classFields (SAClasses.js:194-210) renders ~15 inputs in one modal including 'Form Number' (number), 'Academic Year ID' (number) and 'Track'/'Education Level'/'Category'/'Stream' as free text. The Academic Year field only upgrades to a friendly <select> if /api/school/academic-years/ returns rows (line 282); otherwise the user is asked to type a raw numeric foreign-key ID (line 203, 292).
findings.userImpact: A non-technical school admin sees a long, dense form with an 'Academic Year ID' number box (a DB foreign key) when no academic years are configured, plus several unlabeled-purpose free-text fields. Easy to fill wrong or leave blank; no inline help, grouping, or validation beyond 'name required'.
findings.suggestedFix: Group the form into sections (Identity / Capacity / Schedule), hide or relabel the raw academic_year_id input (never ask for a bare ID — require the dropdown or omit), and add short helper text for Form Number, Track, and Education Level.
findings.backendTrace: Cosmetic/UX only — POST/PUT /api/classes/ (createSuperClass:2409, updateSuperClass:2433) accept all these fields and persist them correctly; no backend defect.

summary: Audited the four school_admin pages in this slice end-to-end (frontend handlers -> ApiClient -> route -> controller -> model). Timetable and Rooms are functional end-to-end (CRUD persists, tenant-scoped). Exams works for creating/listing/deleting exams and entering/saving marks, but the exam "Type" dropdown is a dead control (no DB column, never persisted, list badge renders blank). The single most serious finding is Exam Officers: the page is completely non-functional because the backend returns the wrong response key AND filters out non-officers AND omits the User join the UI needs (name/email), so the list is always empty and no teacher can ever be assigned the Examination Officer role. Security/tenant isolation across the slice is solid: every /api/school/* handler resolves the tenant from the SchoolAdmin link or JWT (getSchoolFromUser/schoolScope) and never trusts a client school_id; mutations are role-gated to school_admin/superadmin via schoolWriteGuard. Note a code-hygiene risk: getExamOfficers/assignExamOfficer are defined twice in schoolController.js (the later duplicate wins).
workingWell: Timetable (timetable-mgr) is functional end-to-end: GET /api/school/timetable/?class_id= reads persisted TimetableSlot rows, POST /generate/ runs a constraint-aware solver in a transaction and bulkCreates slots (no double-booking, max-teacher/day cap, break rows persisted), DELETE clears per-class or whole-school. Response field names line up with the frontend (total_slots->placed, periods_per_day, break_periods).

Rooms (rooms) CRUD is functional and tenant-scoped: getRooms/createRoom/updateRoom/deleteRoom all filter by school.id; toggle reuses updateRoom with is_active; delete uses window.confirm; response key {rooms} matches the UI.

Exams (exam-schedule) core flow works: create/list/delete exams and load/save results all persist and are school-scoped. saveExamResults has a real tenant guard (skips student_ids not in this school) and clamps marks to [0,total_marks].

Tenant isolation is correct across the whole slice: getSchoolFromUser resolves the school from the SchoolAdmin link (or JWT school_id fallback) and never from a client-supplied body/query field; schoolScope only honours ?school_id for superadmin.

Mutations on /api/school/* are role-gated: schoolWriteGuard applies requireRole(['school_admin','superadmin']) to every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, closing the privilege-escalation hole for student/parent/teacher tokens.

Pages use the shared ska- class system whose CSS (SchoolAdmin.css) has @media(max-width:600px/480px/400px/360px) rules collapsing ska-form-grid and ska-stat-grid-4; data tables are wrapped in overflowX:auto so they scroll on mobile.

findings.title: Exam Officers page is permanently empty — backend returns {exam_officers} but UI reads d.teachers
findings.evidence: Frontend SAExtraPages.js:1115-1116 sets state from `d.teachers`: ApiClient.get('/api/school/exam-officers/').then(d => setTeachers(d.teachers || [])). Backend getExamOfficers (schoolController.js:2165-2177, the duplicate that wins) returns successResponse({ exam_officers: officers }) — key is `exam_officers`, never `teachers`. So setTeachers always receives [].
findings.userImpact: A school admin opening Examination Officers sees 'No teachers found' forever. Both the 'Current Examination Officers' section and the 'All Teachers' assignment list are always empty, so they can never assign or remove the Examination Officer role — which the page sub-header says is required to allow report-card generation.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the key the UI expects (rename `exam_officers` -> `teachers`), and have getExamOfficers return ALL teachers (not just officers) with their name/email — see exam-officers-only-returns-officers and exam-officers-missing-user-join. Also delete the duplicate definition.
findings.backendTrace: Route school.js:321 GET /school/exam-officers/ -> getExamOfficers. Two identical definitions exist (schoolController.js:2028 and 2165); JS hoisting/redeclaration means the later one (2165) is the live handler. Both return { exam_officers }.

findings.title: getExamOfficers returns only existing officers, so no NEW officer can ever be assigned
findings.evidence: schoolController.js:2170-2172 (and dup 2033-2035): Teacher.findAll({ where: { school_id: school.id, is_examination_officer: true } }). The query is filtered to officers only. The UI (SAExtraPages.js:1134-1135) splits the returned list into officers = is_examination_officer true and others = false, and renders the 'Assign Role' buttons from `others`. With only officers ever returned, `others` is always empty.
findings.userImpact: Even after fixing the response-key bug, the 'All Teachers' section that lets an admin grant the Examination Officer role would still be empty — there is no path to assign the role to a teacher who does not already have it. The feature is a dead end.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the is_examination_officer filter and return all teachers for the school (the UI does its own officer/non-officer split). Keep the per-school scope.
findings.backendTrace: GET /school/exam-officers/ -> getExamOfficers. assignExamOfficer (schoolController.js:2179) itself works (Teacher.update is_examination_officer scoped by school), but the list it depends on never surfaces non-officers.

findings.title: Exam Officers returns Teacher rows with no name/email (no User join) — UI would crash on t.name.charAt(0)
findings.evidence: Teacher.js has no name/email/first_name columns (grep shows only user_id, employee_id, is_examination_officer, bank_*, emergency_contact_name, next_of_kin_name). getExamOfficers does Teacher.findAll(...) with NO include of User. The UI renders t.name.charAt(0) (SAExtraPages.js:1175,1199), t.name, t.email, t.employee_id (1178-1179,1202-1203). If the list were ever populated, t.name would be undefined and t.name.charAt(0) throws a TypeError, white-screening the page.
findings.userImpact: Compounds the empty-list bug: the only reason the page does not currently crash is that the list is always empty. Fixing the key/filter without also joining User and projecting a `name`/`email` would replace 'empty page' with 'crashed page'.
findings.suggestedFix: In getExamOfficers, include the User association (as 'user') and project name = `${user.first_name} ${user.last_name}`.trim(), email = user.email, employee_id, is_examination_officer, id — mirroring how getSchoolTimetable resolves teacher names (schoolController.js:2346-2347).
findings.backendTrace: GET /school/exam-officers/ -> getExamOfficers (schoolController.js:2165). No include[User]; Teacher model carries no display name.

findings.title: Exam 'Type' dropdown is a dead control — no DB column, never saved, list badge renders blank
findings.evidence: Create form sends exam_type (NewPages.js:280 form default 'final', dropdown 376-379). createExam (schoolController.js:1665) destructures only { term_id, name, date, subject_id, classroom_id, total_marks } and Exam.create omits exam_type. Exam.js has NO exam_type column. getExams (1644-1652) returns no exam_type. The list badge does TYPE_LABEL[e.exam_type] || e.exam_type (NewPages.js:428), which resolves to undefined and renders an empty cyan badge.
findings.userImpact: A school admin carefully picks an exam type (C.A./Mid-Term/Final/Mock/Quiz) when creating an exam, but the choice is silently discarded. Every exam in the list shows a blank Type badge, so the column is useless and the selection is misleading.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an exam_type column to the Exam model + a prod migration, destructure and persist exam_type in createExam, and return it from getExams. If type tracking is not wanted, remove the Type dropdown and the list column to avoid implying data is stored.
findings.backendTrace: POST /school/exams/ -> createExam (schoolController.js:1660) drops exam_type. GET /school/exams/ -> getExams (1628) never selects/returns it. Model pruh_core_exam has no such column.

findings.title: Room 'Notes' field is dropped on create/update — no DB column, yet the table tries to display it
findings.evidence: Room form collects notes (SAExtraPages.js:951,1090-1092) and the table renders {r.notes} under the room name (1040). createRoom (schoolController.js:1615) destructures only { name, code, capacity, room_type } — notes is ignored; updateRoom (1767-1773) builds fields from name/code/capacity/room_type/is_active only. Room.js has no notes column.
findings.userImpact: An admin can type room notes (e.g. 'projector, 2nd floor') and the form accepts them, but they are never saved and never appear in the list. Low impact (cosmetic field) but it is a silent data-loss control.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a notes column to the Room model + migration and persist it in createRoom/updateRoom, or remove the Notes textarea and the table's {r.notes} render so users are not led to enter data that is discarded.
findings.backendTrace: POST/PUT /school/rooms/ -> createRoom (1610) / updateRoom (1761). Neither reads req.body.notes; pruh_core_room has no notes column.

findings.title: Timetable 'Clear' wipes the entire school's timetable with no confirmation when viewing 'All Classes'
findings.evidence: NewPages.js:736-742 handleClear calls ApiClient.delete(`/api/school/timetable/${selClass ? `?class_id=${selClass}` : ''}`) with NO window.confirm. When the View Class selector is set to '— All Classes —' (selClass === '', the default before a class is auto-selected, and an explicit option at 806), the request omits class_id and the backend deleteTimetable (schoolController.js:2452-2459) destroys every TimetableSlot for the school. By contrast Rooms delete, term delete, and assignment delete all use window.confirm.
findings.userImpact: One stray click on 'Clear' while 'All Classes' is selected irreversibly deletes the generated timetable for every class in the school with no warning and no undo. The success banner even reads 'All timetables cleared.' after the fact.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a window.confirm gate to handleClear, with copy that distinguishes single-class vs whole-school clears (e.g. 'Clear the timetable for ALL classes? This cannot be undone.').
findings.backendTrace: DELETE /school/timetable/ -> deleteTimetable (schoolController.js:2452); with no class_id it destroys all slots for school.id. Endpoint works as designed; the gap is the missing client-side confirmation.

findings.title: 'Generate Timetable' always rebuilds ALL classes regardless of the selected View Class
findings.evidence: handleGenerate (NewPages.js:714-734) posts only { periods_per_day, max_teacher_per_day, break_periods } — selClass is never sent. generateTimetable (schoolController.js:2381,2436) loads all active classes for the school, destroys their slots and regenerates them all. The page header/controls are framed around a single 'View Class', so the global scope of Generate is not obvious.
findings.userImpact: An admin who selected one class and tweaks the periods/breaks to regenerate just that class actually wipes and regenerates every class's timetable in the school. Existing manually-acceptable schedules for other classes are silently replaced.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) make the UI explicit that Generate rebuilds the whole school (label it 'Generate All Classes' and warn), or (b) accept an optional class_id in generateTimetable and scope the regenerate to the selected class when one is chosen.
findings.backendTrace: POST /school/timetable/generate/ -> generateTimetable (schoolController.js:2367) operates on all active classes; no class scoping parameter is read.

findings.title: Exam results entry shows hardcoded letter grades, ignoring the school's configured grading scheme
findings.evidence: NewPages.js:480 computes the displayed letter from fixed cutoffs: pct >= 80 'A' : >= 65 'B' : >= 50 'C' : >= 40 'D' : 'F'. These thresholds are hardcoded and do not read the school's Grading Scheme (pass_mark/boundaries) configured at /api/school/grading-scheme/ (GradingSchemePage).
findings.userImpact: While entering marks, the live grade letter an admin sees may not match the school's own grade boundaries (e.g. a school with pass_mark 50 and custom bands). The stored marks are correct, but the on-screen grade preview can mislead. Cosmetic only — letters are not persisted here.
findings.suggestedFix: Fetch the school grading scheme and derive the preview letter from its boundaries, or drop the letter column in the entry view to avoid implying an authoritative grade.
findings.backendTrace: No backend involvement — saveExamResults stores numeric marks only; the letter is a client-side display. Grading scheme available at GET /school/grading-scheme/ but not consumed here.

summary:
The attendance slice (single page `attendance-report` → src/components/principal/AttendanceReport.js) is functional end-to-end and well-built. The one interactive control (the date-range `<select>`: 7/30/90/180 days) is correctly wired: it drives `principalApi.getAttendanceReport(days)` → GET /api/principal/attendance-report/?days=N → controller `getAttendanceReport` in principalController.js (line 442), which aggregates real rows from the `pruh_core_attendance` table (Attendance model), grouped per class with present/absent/late/excused counts and an attendance rate. The data source is real: teachers write attendance via teacherController (`Attendance.upsert`, line 577). Tenant scoping is correct — the controller resolves school via `getSchoolFromUser(req)` which uses `req.schoolId || req.user.school_id` (pinned from JWT for non-superadmin; superadmin may pass ?school_id), so there is NO client-trusted school_id and no cross-tenant leak. The component has proper loading, error, and empty states, sorts low-attendance classes first with a warning banner, and the CSS (AttendanceReport.css) includes the mandated @media(max-width:600px) and (max-width:360px) responsive rules with full-width controls. The ONLY real issue found is a missing role gate on the whole /api/principal/* router: it applies only `authenticateToken` + `schoolScope` and no `requireRole`, so any authenticated user in the school (student, parent, teacher, bursar) can call the attendance-report endpoint and read school-wide attendance analytics meant for principals/school-admins. This is a same-tenant horizontal authorization gap, not a cross-tenant breach.</parameter>
<parameter name="pagesAudited">["attendance-report"]
workingWell: Date-range select (7/30/90/180 days) is fully wired: onChange sets `days`, which re-triggers the memoized `load()` via useEffect, refetching GET /api/principal/attendance-report/?days=N (AttendanceReport.js:54-56, 31-45).
Backend endpoint exists and is real: principal.js:33 routes to getAttendanceReport (principalController.js:442-495), which performs genuine aggregation over the Attendance table — not a stub or mock.
Real data source confirmed: attendance rows are written by teachers via teacherController.js `Attendance.upsert` (line 577), so the report is not perpetually empty by design.

Tenant isolation is correct: getSchoolFromUser uses req.schoolId||req.user.school_id pinned from JWT (principalController.js:19-28; schoolScope.js only honors ?school_id for superadmin), so no cross-tenant exposure and no client-trusted school id.

Complete UX states: distinct error block (AttendanceReport.js:59-65), loading block (67-72), empty block with helpful copy (74-80), plus low-attendance warning banner (107-112) and low classes sorted first (controller sort at line 479).
Responsive: AttendanceReport.css has @media(max-width:600px) stacking the header and making the select full-width (97-116) and @media(max-width:360px) (118-120), meeting the project mobile mandate.
Defensive client parsing: handles res.success===false, null overall, and overall.total===0 without crashing (AttendanceReport.js:36-39, 74, 82).

findings.title: Attendance report endpoint (and all /api/principal/*) lacks a requireRole gate — any authenticated user can read school-wide attendance
findings.evidence: principal.js:15-18 applies only `router.use(authenticateToken)` and `router.use(schoolScope)` — there is NO `requireRole(...)`. auth.js:6-46 only validates the JWT and sets req.user; it does not restrict role. schoolScope.js:1-11 only pins school_id, no role check. The route principal.js:33 `router.get('/attendance-report/', getAttendanceReport)` therefore accepts any valid token. By contrast requireRole IS used on sibling routers: finance.js:55/57, school.js:152, superadmin.js:112/227. getAttendanceReport (principalController.js:442) resolves the school from the caller's own JWT and returns full school-wide present/absent/late/excused counts per class.
findings.userImpact: A logged-in student, parent, teacher, or bursar in the same school can call GET /api/principal/attendance-report/ directly (e.g. via devtools/curl with their own token) and retrieve principal-level, school-wide attendance analytics for every class — data the UI never exposes to them and that is intended for principals/school admins. No cross-tenant leak (school is pinned to the caller's own school), but it is a cross-role information disclosure within the tenant.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a role gate on the principal router, e.g. `router.use(requireRole(['principal','school_admin','superadmin']))` after schoolScope in principal.js (mirroring finance.js/school.js). If specific principal endpoints must stay broader, gate per-route instead. Re-verify that legitimate school_admin/principal tokens still pass (they carry role 'school_admin'/'principal').
findings.backendTrace: GET /api/principal/attendance-report/?days=N → mounted at index.js:142 (app.use('/api/principal', principalRouter)) → principal.js:15-18 (authenticateToken + schoolScope only, no requireRole) → principal.js:33 getAttendanceReport → principalController.js:442-495 (real aggregation over Attendance where school_id = caller's school). Endpoint EXISTS and WORKS; the gap is authorization, not functionality.

summary: The virtual-meetings slice is a single component (SAVirtualMeeting.js) reused for three audiences (parents/staffs/students). The admin-side CRUD is genuinely functional end-to-end and well-secured: all four routes (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/virtual-meetings/) are gated by [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])], the controller pins school_admin to their own school via scopedSchoolId() (-1 sentinel prevents cross-tenant leakage when no school_id) and guards update/delete with outsideScope() to prevent IDOR, and every UI control (Schedule, Edit, Delete with confirm modal, Complete, Cancel, Join link, plus the superadmin school filter) maps to a real handler that persists to pruh_core_virtual_meeting. Empty/loading/error/toast states are all present and the CSS is fully responsive (42px+ touch targets, @media max-width:600px). The real problems are at the product level, not the plumbing: (1) the feature is admin-create-only — NO parent, staff, or student portal anywhere consumes VirtualMeeting, so the audience never sees the meeting or its join link; (2) the page subtitle promises 'reminders' but no notification/email is ever generated; (3) the model relies on db.sync alter which is OFF in production, and no .sql migration exists, so the prod table must be created by hand or every call 500s.
workingWell: Role gating is correct: all four /api/virtual-meetings/ routes carry sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])] (superadmin.js:227, 329-332). A teacher/parent/student token is rejected with 403.

Tenant isolation is solid: scopedSchoolId() pins a school_admin to their own school and returns -1 (matches nothing) when the token has no school_id (superadminDataController.js:55-60); getVirtualMeetings filters where.school_id accordingly (1688); update/delete additionally call outsideScope() so a school_admin cannot edit/delete another school's meeting even by guessing an id — returns 404 (1735, 1756). No IDOR.

createVirtualMeeting ignores client-supplied school_id for non-superadmin (forcedSchool wins; data.school_id only used when forcedSchool is null i.e. superadmin), so a school_admin cannot plant a meeting in another tenant (1709-1711).

Full CRUD is real and persists: create/list/update/delete all hit the DB; status transitions (scheduled/completed/cancelled) are whitelisted server-side (1742). The Complete/Cancel buttons and the Edit-form status dropdown all work end-to-end.

Every interactive control is wired: Schedule Meeting (line 158), Edit/Delete icon buttons (123-124), Delete confirm modal (207-218), Complete/Cancel (140-141), Join link (135-136, opens meeting_url in new tab with rel=noopener), and the superadmin-only school <select> filter (280-288). No dead buttons.

Good UX states: loading spinner (163), error banner (164), empty state (168-173), per-section empty text (179), and a toast system (151, 63) for success/error feedback. Upcoming vs Past split is computed sensibly (86-96).

Fully responsive per project mandate: SAVirtualMeeting.css:191-199 has @media (max-width:600px) collapsing the grid and form to one column, full-width buttons, and column-reversed modal actions; touch targets are >=42px (.savm-btn min-height 42px, inputs min-height 42px, mobile buttons 46px).
MeetingForm is conditionally mounted, so opening 'Schedule' after an 'Edit' starts from a clean useState({duration_minutes:60}) — no stale-form bug between create and edit.

findings.title: Scheduled meetings are never delivered to parents/staff/students — admin-only data island
findings.evidence: Grep for VirtualMeeting/virtual-meetings across the whole frontend returns ONLY SuperadminDashboard.js, SAVirtualMeeting.js and SAVirtualMeeting.css. Across the whole backend it returns ONLY superadminDataController.js, models/VirtualMeeting.js and routes/superadmin.js. parentController.js has zero references. There is no parent/teacher/student endpoint or portal view that lists VirtualMeeting rows. The component header comment (lines 4-9) and subtitle 'Schedule and manage video meetings for X. Shareable join links, reminders and status tracking.' (line 156) imply the audience receives the meeting, but nothing on the parent/staff/student side ever reads these rows.
findings.userImpact: A school admin fills in a Parent-Teacher Meeting with a Google Meet/Zoom link and a time, sees 'Meeting scheduled', and reasonably believes parents will get the invite/link. In reality the meeting lives only in the admin's own dashboard. No parent, staff member, or student is ever shown the meeting or the join link, so the core purpose of the feature (getting an audience into a video call) does not happen. The admin must copy the link out-of-band, defeating the tool.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a read endpoint and UI on the consumer side: parent portal lists VirtualMeeting where audience='parents' AND school_id=their school (status='scheduled'); teacher/staff portal for audience='staffs'; student portal for audience='students'. Surface upcoming meetings with the Join link on each role's overview/notifications page so the audience can actually attend.
findings.backendTrace: VirtualMeeting model (models/VirtualMeeting.js) + CRUD in superadminDataController.js getVirtualMeetings/createVirtualMeeting (lines 1683-1729). No GET handler in parentController.js / teacher / student controllers reads VirtualMeeting. Backend grep confirms only 3 files reference it, all admin-side.

findings.title: UI advertises 'reminders' but no reminder/notification is ever created
findings.evidence: Subtitle at SAVirtualMeeting.js:156 reads '...Shareable join links, reminders and status tracking.' But createVirtualMeeting (superadminDataController.js:1704-1729) only does VirtualMeeting.create({...}) and returns — no Notification row, no email, no SMS, no scheduled job. updateVirtualMeeting (1731-1750) likewise only mutates the row. There is no reminder mechanism anywhere in the slice.
findings.userImpact: The admin trusts the product's own copy that attendees will be reminded. No reminder is ever sent (and per the previous finding, attendees can't even see the meeting). The promised behaviour silently does not exist, so admins may skip manually notifying people and attendance suffers.
findings.suggestedFix: Either implement reminders (create Notification rows / queue email on create and N minutes before scheduled_at), or remove the word 'reminders' from line 156 until it is real. Do not advertise capabilities the code does not have.
findings.backendTrace: createVirtualMeeting / updateVirtualMeeting in superadminDataController.js — no notification/email side effects present.

findings.title: pruh_core_virtual_meeting has no production migration; depends on dev-only db.sync(alter)
findings.evidence: VirtualMeeting.js:22 tableName 'pruh_core_virtual_meeting'. index.js:154 runs db.sync({ alter: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' }) — alter is DISABLED in production. A repo grep for *.sql referencing virtual_meeting returns nothing, so there is no manual migration shipped for this table (consistent with the project's documented 'pending prod migrations' pattern for TimetableSlot etc.). Locally the table auto-creates; in prod it will not exist unless created by hand.
findings.userImpact: On production, the first time a school admin opens any vm-* page or clicks Schedule, the query against a non-existent table throws and the handler returns 500 'Internal server error' (caught at lines 1698-1701 / 1725-1728). The admin sees 'HTTP 500' in the error/toast and the entire feature is dead until ops runs a CREATE TABLE by hand.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a committed SQL migration that creates pruh_core_virtual_meeting (mirroring the model columns) and run it on prod, the same way TimetableSlot and academic-year ALTERs are handled. Document it in the pending-prod-migrations list.
findings.backendTrace: Model maps to pruh_core_virtual_meeting; index.js:154 sync alter off in prod; no .sql file creates the table; controller wraps errors as 500.

findings.title: Meeting can be saved with no link and no date; client-only validation accepts empty join URL and past times
findings.evidence: MeetingForm.submit (SAVirtualMeeting.js:253-268) only enforces title ('Title is required.', line 256). meeting_url and scheduled_at are optional; payload sends them as '' / null. Backend createVirtualMeeting (superadminDataController.js:1704-1724) validates only data.title; it never validates meeting_url is a URL or scheduled_at is present/future. The card then renders no Join button when meeting_url is empty (line 135) and 'Not scheduled' when scheduled_at is null (fmtWhen, line 44).
findings.userImpact: An admin can create a 'meeting' with no link and no time and it is accepted as scheduled. The resulting card has nothing to join and shows 'Not scheduled', which is a dead card. Past-dated meetings silently drop into the 'Past & Closed' bucket (upcoming/past split, lines 86-96) even though just created, which looks like a bug to the admin.
findings.suggestedFix: Require scheduled_at and a valid http(s) meeting_url in the form before enabling Schedule (and mirror the check server-side in createVirtualMeeting). Warn when the chosen time is in the past.
findings.backendTrace: createVirtualMeeting validates only title (line 1707); accepts null scheduled_at and empty meeting_url.

summary: The ai-capture slice is one page: schooladmin/AIDocumentCapture.js (nav key 'ai-capture', rendered at SuperadminDashboard.js:1505) backed by POST /api/school/ai-capture/ and GET /api/school/ai-capture/list/. The BACKEND is solid and end-to-end correct: both routes use applyAuth (authenticateToken + requireActiveAccount + schoolScope + schoolWriteGuard); the POST is a mutating method so schoolWriteGuard enforces requireRole(['school_admin','superadmin']); schoolScope pins req.schoolId from the JWT (never trusted from client) and the controller writes/reads AIDocumentCapture WHERE school_id = that value, so tenant isolation holds. The prior audit's 'committed Gemini key' concern is RESOLVED — aiCaptureController.js and syllabusGenerator.js both read GEMINI_API_KEY from process.env only, with a clean 503 when unset; no key is committed. The model auto-creates in dev (controller require registers it before db.sync) and the documented production migration covers prod. HOWEVER there is a CRITICAL client-integration bug: adminApi.aiCaptureUpload() returns apiClient.request(...) which resolves to the RAW fetch Response object (not parsed JSON), yet the component reads r.success / r.structured / r.capture_id — all undefined on a Response. Result: even a fully successful 200 extraction takes the else branch and shows 'AI extraction failed.', and the extracted-rows preview table NEVER renders. The feature is effectively non-functional from the user's seat despite a working backend. Secondary issues: multer rejects (oversized/bad-type) on this route bubble to Express's default handler as non-JSON (no error middleware exists), and there is no frontend file-size guard against the 25MB cap; minor responsiveness gap (the .aidc wrapper has no CSS, leans entirely on shared ska-* classes + overflowX scroll, which is acceptable but untcustomized).
workingWell: Backend route POST /api/school/ai-capture/ is fully gated: applyAuth (school.js:159,275) runs authenticateToken + requireActiveAccount + schoolScope + schoolWriteGuard, and because POST is a mutating method schoolWriteGuard (school.js:150-155) calls requireRole(['school_admin','superadmin']). No TODO_JWT backdoor on this route.

Tenant isolation is correct: schoolScope (schoolScope.js:3-4) sets req.schoolId = req.user.school_id from the JWT for non-superadmin; aiCaptureUpload (aiCaptureController.js:131) and aiCaptureList (aiCaptureController.js:178,182) use that server-derived schoolId for both the INSERT and the list WHERE clause, so a school admin can never read or write another tenant's captures.

No committed AI key (prior-audit concern resolved): aiCaptureController.js:7-8 and syllabusGenerator.js:9-10 both read GEMINI_API_KEY from process.env only and return a clean 503 'not configured' when unset (aiCaptureController.js:124-126). grep for an AIza* literal across the repo and .env files found nothing.

Controller does real work and is robust: extracts text from PDF/DOCX/TXT/CSV or sends images to Gemini multimodal (aiCaptureController.js:90-114), persists a processing→done/failed audit row with rows_count and error (aiCaptureController.js:139-156,168-170), and always unlinks the temp upload via cleanup() on every path (aiCaptureController.js:119-120,157,166).

Schema lifecycle is covered: AIDocumentCapture model auto-creates in dev because requiring schoolRouter (index.js:14) transitively requires the controller and model before db.sync({alter}) runs (index.js:154); production is covered by the documented migration 2026-06-23-ai-capture-and-expense-approval.sql (CREATE TABLE pruh_school_ai_document_capture).

The capture-history table (GET .../list/) is wired correctly end-to-end: aiCaptureList uses apiClient.get (returns parsed JSON), the component reads d.success/d.captures, and renders status pills + rows + error notes (AIDocumentCapture.js:24-26,168-208).

findings.title: Upload result is a raw fetch Response, not JSON — every successful extraction shows 'AI extraction failed.' and the preview never renders
findings.evidence: adminApi.js:19-23 — aiCaptureUpload() does `return apiClient.request('/api/school/ai-capture/', { method:'POST', body: fd })`. apiClient.request() resolves to the RAW fetch Response object (client.js:154 `return response;`), it does NOT call .json(). The component then does `const r = await adminApi.aiCaptureUpload(...)` and `if (r.success) { setResult(r); ... } else { setErr(r.message || 'AI extraction failed.') }` (AIDocumentCapture.js:39-45). A Response object has no `.success`, `.message`, `.structured`, or `.capture_id` properties, so r.success is undefined → the else branch always runs → setErr('AI extraction failed.'). Even on a 200 with extracted rows, the rows preview block (AIDocumentCapture.js:120-165, keyed on `result`) never renders because setResult is never reached. Contrast aiCaptureList (adminApi.js:24-26) which correctly uses apiClient.get (returns parsed JSON) and works.
findings.userImpact: A school admin uploads a roster/grade/attendance file, the backend successfully calls Gemini and saves the rows, but the UI shows a red 'Error: AI extraction failed.' and never displays the extracted table. The history row will say status 'done' with a row count, directly contradicting the error message the admin just saw. The core feature of the page is unusable from the user's perspective despite the backend working.
findings.suggestedFix: Parse the response in adminApi.aiCaptureUpload: `const res = await apiClient.request('/api/school/ai-capture/', { method:'POST', body: fd }); return res.json();` (mirror the get/post helpers). Same fix applies to adminApi.bulkImport (adminApi.js:34) which has the identical raw-Response bug. Alternatively expose a postForm helper on apiClient that handles FormData and returns .json().
findings.backendTrace: POST /api/school/ai-capture/ (school.js:275) → applyAuth → aiCaptureMulter.single('file') → aiCaptureUpload (aiCaptureController.js:117). Endpoint EXISTS, is role-gated and tenant-scoped, and returns a correct JSON body { success:true, capture_id, structured:{rows,columns} } (aiCaptureController.js:159-164). The defect is purely on the frontend integration layer, not the backend.

findings.title: Multer rejects (oversized / unsupported file) return non-JSON and surface as an opaque 'HTTP 500' to the admin
findings.evidence: The route mounts multer directly: `router.post('/school/ai-capture/', applyAuth, aiCaptureMulter.single('file'), aiCaptureUpload)` (school.js:275) with a 25MB limit and a fileFilter that throws on bad types (school.js:256-274). Unlike teacherUpload/studentUpload (school.js:91-131) which wrap multer and convert errors to `res.status(400).json(...)`, this route has no such wrapper, and index.js has NO Express error-handling middleware — only a 404 handler (index.js:162-168). So a multer LIMIT_FILE_SIZE or fileFilter error bubbles to Express's default handler, which returns an HTML error page, not JSON. The client then fails `response.clone().json()` (client.js:131-138) and falls back to `HTTP <status>: <statusText>` (client.js:129). Frontend also has no size check before upload (AIDocumentCapture.js:30-50 just sets the file).
findings.userImpact: An admin who picks a file over 25MB, or a slightly off mimetype that slips past the .accept filter, gets a meaningless 'HTTP 500' / generic network error instead of a clear 'file too large (max 25MB)' or 'unsupported file type' message — with no guidance on what to fix.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap aiCaptureMulter like teacherUpload/studentUpload to translate LIMIT_FILE_SIZE and filter errors into res.status(400).json({success:false, message}); and/or add a global Express error-handling middleware in index.js that JSON-ifies multer/other errors. Add a client-side size guard in onPick (reject >25MB with a friendly message).
findings.backendTrace: aiCaptureMulter (school.js:256-274) limits to 25MB and filters mimetype/extension. On rejection the error is not caught by any handler (no app.use((err,req,res,next)) in index.js), so Express default HTML response is sent.

findings.title: AIDocumentCapture has no dedicated CSS and no own @media rules; relies entirely on shared ska-* classes + inline styles
findings.evidence: The root wrapper uses className 'aidc' (AIDocumentCapture.js:62) but a grep for '.aidc' across all of src returned zero CSS matches — the class is purely a hook with no styling. All layout is inline styles plus shared ska-card/ska-input/ska-btn classes (which do carry @media rules in SchoolAdmin.css). The two data tables set fixed inline fontSize 0.8rem and rely on a parent `overflowX:'auto'` wrapper (AIDocumentCapture.js:129-130,173) for horizontal scroll on mobile, and the uploader row uses flexWrap:'wrap' (AIDocumentCapture.js:73). There are no component-specific max-width:600px rules as the project standard mandates.
findings.userImpact: On a phone the wide extracted-rows / history tables scroll horizontally (functional but cramped); the uploader controls wrap acceptably. No layout break, but the page is not tuned for small screens the way the standing mobile-responsiveness rule requires.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small .aidc stylesheet (or rules in SchoolAdmin.css) with @media (max-width:600px): reduce table cell padding, ensure the file input and select are full-width, and confirm 44px touch targets on the Extract/Reset buttons; keep the overflowX scroll wrappers as the fallback for wide tables.

summary:
Audited the cross-cutting backend that powers the school_admin finance, attendance, report-card, and virtual-meeting pages: routes/finance.js + controllers/financeController.js, routes/principal.js + controllers/principalController.js, routes/live-classes.js + the live-class methods in studentController.js, plus the /api/virtual-meetings/ handlers in superadminDataController.js, and every frontend consumer (financeApi.js, adminApi.js, SAVirtualMeeting.js, bursar/* and principal/* pages). The page-level UX is largely solid end-to-end (VM CRUD, AttendanceReport, FeeCategories, RecordPaymentModal all have real queries plus loading/empty/error states and are correctly token-scoped). The serious problems are at the route layer: the entire /api/principal/* router and almost all of /api/finance/* have NO requireRole and NO requireActiveAccount middleware. They scope by school_id from the token, so they are not cross-tenant, but they are NOT role-gated: any authenticated user who carries a school_id (a teacher, parent, or student) can read the school's finance/analytics and POST to publish report cards, approve/reject grades, record payments, assign fees, and create principal/finance staff accounts. This is a horizontal/vertical privilege-escalation hole the rest of the codebase guards against (the sibling /api/* school CRUD routes use `sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])]`, and finance expense record/review correctly use requireRole — but the other 20+ finance/principal mutations do not). Two write paths also trust client-supplied IDs (assignFees, recordPayment) without confirming the fee category / fee belongs to the caller's school. Separately, BursarHome's quick-action buttons navigate a school_admin to bursar-only page keys through goTo(), which never checks canAccess, so the permission model is bypassed in the UI. live-classes create/update/delete are also ungated.</parameter>
<parameter name="pagesAudited">["fee-dashboard","fee-categories","school-financial-report","report-cards-published","syllabus-progress","attendance-report","vm-parents","vm-staffs","vm-students","finance-users"]
workingWell: Virtual Meeting (vm-parents/vm-staffs/vm-students) is fully functional end-to-end: SAVirtualMeeting.js CRUD wires to /api/virtual-meetings/ which is role-gated by `sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])]` (superadmin.js:329-332) and tenant-pinned via scopedSchoolId/outsideScope (superadminDataController.js:1686,1735,1756). Has loading, empty, error and toast states.

AttendanceReport (attendance-report) is clean: principal/AttendanceReport.js calls /api/principal/attendance-report/?days= → getAttendanceReport (principalController.js:442) runs a real school-scoped aggregation with day clamping (max 365) and renders loading/empty/error/low-attendance states.

FeeCategories (fee-categories) end-to-end works: create modal validates amount>0, calls financeApi.createFeeCategory → createFeeCategory (financeController.js:260) which pins school_id; list has skeleton loading, CTA empty state and error banner.

Expense workflow has correct separation-of-duties: POST /api/finance/expenses/ is requireRole(CAN_RECORD_EXPENSE) and POST /api/finance/expenses/:id/review/ is requireRole(CAN_APPROVE_EXPENSE) with an individual-level self-approval guard (financeController.js:628) and 409 on already-reviewed.

RecordPaymentModal is robust: client-side amount/balance validation, student/fee picker, success receipt with integrity hash; recordPayment runs in a transaction and updates the linked fee status atomically (financeController.js:350-416).
Impersonation write-audit trail is in place: auth.js:34-43 logs every mutating request made under a superadmin impersonation token.

findings.title: Entire /api/principal/* router has no role gate — any authenticated user can publish report cards, approve/reject grades, and create principal accounts
findings.evidence: principal.js:15-36 mounts only `router.use(authenticateToken); router.use(schoolScope);` then exposes POST /report-cards/ (publishReportCard), POST /grade-approvals/ (reviewGradeChange), POST /report-cards/comment/, and POST/PUT /principal-users/ with NO requireRole and NO requireActiveAccount. getSchoolFromUser (principalController.js:19-28) returns a school for ANY token that carries school_id (teacher/parent/student all do), so role is never checked. Contrast the sibling shared CRUD which uses `sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin'])]` (superadmin.js:227).
findings.userImpact: A teacher, parent, or student of the school can call POST /api/principal/report-cards/ to publish report cards, POST /api/principal/grade-approvals/ to approve or reject grade-change requests (writing immutable grade-audit events as if they were the principal), and POST /api/principal/principal-users/ to mint a brand-new principal login. Grade integrity and report-card release — the most sensitive academic actions — are unprotected against any logged-in school member.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `const requireRole = require('../middleware/requireRole'); const requireActiveAccount = require('../middleware/requireActiveAccount');` and gate the router: `router.use(authenticateToken, schoolScope, requireActiveAccount, requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin','principal']));` (read endpoints can include bursar where appropriate). Mirror the `sla` pattern already used in superadmin.js.
findings.backendTrace: routes/principal.js:15-36 → controllers/principalController.js publishReportCard:256 / reviewGradeChange:128 / createPrincipalUser:359 — all execute real writes (transactions + appendGradeEvent) with no role check upstream.

findings.title: Most /api/finance/* mutations have no role gate — any authenticated user can record payments, assign fees, and create finance/bursar accounts
findings.evidence: finance.js:23-26 applies only authenticateToken + schoolScope. requireRole is imported and used on lines 55 and 57 (expenses only). Everything else — POST /payments/ (recordPayment:350), POST /fees/assign/ (assignFees:298), POST /fee-categories/ (createFeeCategory:260), POST /finance-users/ + PUT /finance-users/:id/ (createFinanceUser:696 / updateFinanceUser:732), GET /stats|analytics|fees|payments|overview — has NO requireRole and NO requireActiveAccount. getSchoolFromUser (financeController.js:24-33) resolves a school for any token with school_id.
findings.userImpact: Any logged-in member of the school (teacher/parent/student) can read full finance analytics and debtor lists, record arbitrary payments against students, assign fees, and create a new bursar user account (createFinanceUser hashes a default password and inserts a SchoolAdmin row). They could fabricate payment receipts or grant themselves a finance login. The fact that only expense record/review were gated shows the gating was applied unevenly.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate the whole router the same way: `router.use(authenticateToken, schoolScope, requireActiveAccount); router.use(requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin','principal','bursar']));` then keep the stricter per-route requireRole on the expense approve/reject (school leadership only). Read-only GETs can share the broad gate; account-creation POSTs should be narrowed to ['superadmin','school_admin'].
findings.backendTrace: routes/finance.js:42-54 → recordPayment / assignFees / createFinanceUser all perform real DB writes with no role enforcement.

findings.title: Finance and principal routers skip requireActiveAccount, so a suspended/rejected school_admin keeps full access
findings.evidence: The shared school CRUD deliberately re-checks approval per request via `sla = [requireActiveAccount, requireRole(...)]` (superadmin.js:224-227, comment: 'a suspended/rejected school_admin is blocked immediately even with a still-valid token'). Neither finance.js nor principal.js include requireActiveAccount in their `router.use(...)` chain (finance.js:23-26, principal.js:15-18).
findings.userImpact: A school_admin whose school was suspended or whose account was deactivated still holds a valid JWT and can continue to record payments, approve grades, publish report cards, and manage staff through the finance/principal endpoints until the token expires — defeating the suspension control that the rest of the platform enforces.
findings.suggestedFix: Add requireActiveAccount to the router.use chain on both finance.js and principal.js (after authenticateToken/schoolScope), matching the `sla` pattern.
findings.backendTrace: middleware/requireActiveAccount.js:26 exists and is used by superadmin.js but is never wired into finance.js or principal.js.

findings.title: assignFees and recordPayment trust client-supplied fee_category_id / fee_id without verifying they belong to the caller's school
findings.evidence: assignFees: `const category = await FeeCategory.findByPk(fee_category_id);` (financeController.js:309) — no school_id filter; the created Fee rows are then stamped with the caller's school.id (line 325). recordPayment: `const fee = await Fee.findByPk(fee_id, { transaction });` (financeController.js:377) — no school_id check before mutating fee.amount_paid/status. student_id is likewise taken from the body and never confirmed to be in school.id.
findings.userImpact: A school_admin (or, given the missing role gate above, any school member) can pass another school's fee_category_id or fee_id. assignFees would copy a foreign category's amount into their own school's fee ledger; recordPayment would mutate another tenant's Fee row (advancing amount_paid / flipping status to paid) — cross-tenant data corruption driven by a guessable integer id.
findings.suggestedFix: Scope every client-supplied id to the resolved school: `FeeCategory.findOne({ where: { id: fee_category_id, school_id: school.id } })`, `Fee.findOne({ where: { id: fee_id, school_id: school.id } })`, and validate student_id belongs to school.id before creating Fee/Payment rows. Return 404 when the id is outside the tenant.
findings.backendTrace: financeController.js assignFees:298-348 and recordPayment:350-416 — both create/mutate rows after an unscoped findByPk.

findings.title: live-classes create/update/delete are ungated — any authenticated user can create or remove a school's live classes
findings.evidence: live-classes.js:11-16 applies only `router.use(authenticateToken)` then POST/PATCH/DELETE map to createLiveClass/updateLiveClass/deleteLiveClass. createLiveClass (studentController.js:2168) reads class_id/subject_id from the body, sets school_id from the token and `teacher_id: req.user.id` for any role, with no requireRole. update/delete scope only by school_id (studentController.js:2193,2206).
findings.userImpact: A parent or student token can POST /api/live-classes/ to create a live class for any class in their school (and is recorded as the teacher), or DELETE existing ones. No school_admin UI exposes this (adminApi.listLiveClasses at adminApi.js:41 is a dead helper with no consumer), but the endpoints are reachable by any authenticated user.
findings.suggestedFix: Add requireRole(['superadmin','school_admin','principal','teacher']) to the write routes in live-classes.js, and validate that class_id/subject_id belong to the caller's school in createLiveClass.
findings.backendTrace: routes/live-classes.js:13-16 → studentController.js createLiveClass:2168 / updateLiveClass:2190 / deleteLiveClass:2203 — writes with no role check.

findings.title: Finance Command Center quick actions send a school_admin to bursar-only pages, bypassing the permission model
findings.evidence: BursarHome QUICK_ACTIONS (BursarHome.js:17-25) call navigateTo('payments'|'expenses'|'student-fees'|'finance-team'|'finance-reports'). navigateTo is goTo (SuperadminDashboard.js:622-623) which is just `setActivePage(page)` with NO canAccess check. Those keys render real components via the switch (SuperadminDashboard.js:1469-1474) and are in HANDLED_PAGES (line 376), but in permissions.js they are BURSAR-only (payments:121, expenses:122, student-fees:114, finance-team:115, finance-reports:116) — not granted to school_admin.
findings.userImpact: A school_admin who opens the fee-dashboard and clicks 'All Payments', 'Record Expense', 'Student Fees', 'Finance Team', or 'Reports' is navigated to pages the permission config says they cannot access. They load (data is token-scoped so it is their own school, not a leak), but the permission system is silently bypassed and the page has no sidebar entry, leaving the admin on a screen with no nav highlight and no documented access path. It also makes the permission matrix untrustworthy.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) make goTo enforce canAccess and no-op/redirect when the role lacks the key, or (b) intentionally add these finance keys to school_admin in permissions.js and give them sidebar entries. Decide one source of truth; today the render switch and the permission config disagree.
findings.backendTrace: N/A (frontend routing/permission mismatch). Underlying /api/finance/* calls succeed because they are token-scoped.

findings.title: Fee categories can be created but never edited or deactivated — no update/delete endpoint or UI
findings.evidence: financeApi exposes only getFeeCategories and createFeeCategory (financeApi.js:62-73) with the explicit comment 'GET/POST only — no update/delete route'. finance.js has only GET/POST /fee-categories/ (lines 49-50). The FeeCategories card renders an is_active badge (FeeCategories.js:222-224) but there is no control to toggle it and no PUT/DELETE route to back one.
findings.userImpact: Once a school_admin creates a fee category with a wrong amount/name, they cannot edit, deactivate, or delete it — they can only create a new one, leaving stale/incorrect categories permanently in the picker. The Active/Inactive badge implies a toggle that does not exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Add PUT /api/finance/fee-categories/:id/ and DELETE (or a toggle) in finance.js + financeController, and surface edit/deactivate controls on the card. If deactivation is intended, persist is_active and respect it when listing categories for assignment.
